sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Renuka Yara
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2459 of 2019
Judgment:

This appeal is directed against the order dated 14.12.2018 passed in M.V.O.P.No.2705 of 2013 by the learned Motor Accidents Tribunal-cum-III Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short, 'the Tribunal'), seeking just compensation along with interest at 18% per annum and for costs.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Tribunal-cum-III Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts that led to filing of this appeal are that the appellants/claimants have filed the claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- from the respondents herein jointly and severally, on account of death of one late S.Narsimlu in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.06.2013, upon being hit by a vehicle bearing registration No.AP-09-P-6104 belonging to Begum Bazar P.S.
The Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.7,85,750/- with interest at 7.5% per annum.
3. The details of the subject accident and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.

The claimants have preferred the present appeal only seeking enhancement of compensation, relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 1, wherein, it was held that future prospects and statutory benefits such as consortium, love and affection, funeral expenses and loss of estate to a tune of Rs.70,000/- ought to be awarded to the claimants therein.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The claimants also relied on A.I.Muthaiah v. Rathod Redya 2,
wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme court held that compensation exceeding the claim amount can be granted.

Lastly, the claimants relied on a judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sayed Sadiq v.
Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited 3, wherein the notional income of the fruit vendor is taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.

entities.text:
Sayed Sadiq v.
Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Contending that the deceased S.Narsimlu was working as watchman as on the date of the subject accident, the claimants sought a compensation of Rs.15,22,500/- by taking notional income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- per month and to add future prospects at 25% and 10% increase on statutory benefits.
4.
Upon considering the claim, it is seen that the avocation of the deceased S.Narsimlu is shown to be that of a watchman in the FIR and the inquest report.
The Tribunal had taken Rs.4,500/- per month as the notional income of the deceased as a watchman.
The income of an unskilled labour might be taken at Rs.4,500/- per month.
Since the deceased was a watchman, this Court deems it just and proper to 2017 ACJ 2700 2015(4) ALD 585 2014 SCC 735 take his notional income as Rs.6,000/- per month in the year 2013.
After adding 25% of future prospects, his monthly notional income comes to Rs.7,500/-.
Since there are 4 dependents on the deceased, 1/4th of his monthly income is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Thus, the notional income of the deceased comes to Rs.5,625/- per month and Rs.67,500/- per annum (Rs.5,625/- x 12).

The appropriate multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Smt. S. Pochamma And 3 Others vs Government Of Andhra Pradesh And 2 ... on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189489124/

sentences.text: Smt. Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 4 is '14'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the loss of income comes to Rs.9,45,000/- (Rs.67,500/- x 14).

The claimants are also entitled to Rs.70,000/- towards loss of consortium, love and affection, funeral expenses and loss of estate, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (1 supra).
Further, the claim petition was filed in the year 2013.
Therefore, 10% increase is to be added to the statutory benefits of Rs.70,000/-, which comes to Rs.7,000/-.

Further, considering the fact that the claimant Nos.2 to 4 being the children of the deceased, this Court is inclined to award a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of parental consortium as per the decision of the Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited v.
Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and 2009(6)SCC 121 others 5.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Company Limited v.
Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and 2009(6)SCC 121 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the total loss of income comes to Rs.11,54,000/- (Rs.9,45,000/-+ Rs.77,000/- and Rs.44,000/- x 3).

5. In view of the Judgments of the Apex Court in Laxman @ Laxman Mourya Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 6 and Nagappa Vs. Gurudayal Singh 7,
the claimants are entitled to get more amount than what has been claimed.

entities.text: Laxman @ Laxman Mourya Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and another 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Motor Vehicles Act being a beneficial piece of legislation, where the interest of the claimants is a paramount consideration the Courts should always endeavour to extend the benefit to the claimants to a just and reasonable extent.
6. Accordingly, M.A.C.M.A. is allowed.
The compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is hereby enhanced from Rs.7,85,750/- to Rs.11,54,000/-.
However, the appellants shall pay the deficit Court Fee on the enhanced compensation.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The enhanced amount shall be apportioned among the claimants in the same proportion in which original compensation amounts were directed by the Tribunal.

The time for depositing the said amount by the respondents jointly and severally is two months from the date of (2018) 18 SCC 130 (2011) 10 SCC 756 2003 ACJ 12 (SC)
receipt of a copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the major claimants are permitted to withdraw their respective share amounts without furnishing any security.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this appeal, shall stand closed.
